messages:
jess_sec: Auditor emailed asking for a minimal 'proof bundle' that cleanly ties a single RBAC change to: git commit -> CI apply -> k8s audit log -> cloud audit (CloudTrail) -> KMS metadata. They want a short replay and a CSV crosswalk to SOC2/ISO controls.
harry_oncall: Ok. We should keep it scoped: one service account, one rolebinding in staging, one CI pipeline run. Capture the commit SHA, pipeline ID, and kube-apiserver audit lines.
auditor_sam: Staging is fine. Please ensure all IDs and hostnames are redacted. A 60s screencast showing the apply -> logs is perfect, plus the exact queries/commands you used.
leo_platform: I'll create a disposable SA (sa-audit-demo) and an ephemeral rolebinding limited to namespace 'staging-demo'. I'll record the kubectl apply, the controller events, and the CI job that applied it. I'll tear everything down after the demo.
jess_sec: Paste the exact extraction commands you'll include in the README so the auditor can reproduce the mapping.
leo_platform: K8s audit extraction (example snippet we'll include; will parameterize namespace and binding name):
```bash
# extract audit events referencing the rolebinding
jq -c 'select(.objectRef.resource=="rolebindings" and .objectRef.namespace=="staging-demo")' /var/log/kube-apiserver/audit.log | sed -n '1,50p'
```
CloudTrail/console events we'll export via the AWS CLI and include a CSV:
```bash
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=PutRolePolicy \
  --start-time 2024-11-01 --end-time 2024-11-30 --output json > cloudtrail-putrolepolicy.json
jq -r '.Events[] | [.EventTime, .Username, .EventName, .Resources[]?.ResourceName, .CloudTrailEvent] | @csv' cloudtrail-putrolepolicy.json > cloudtrail-putrolepolicy.csv
```
KMS proof commands (staging key):
```bash
aws kms describe-key --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/EXAMPLE-STAGING --profile staging > kms-describe.json
aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/EXAMPLE-STAGING --profile staging > kms-rotation.json
```
leo_platform: CI tie-in (we'll include pipeline ID and commit):
```bash
# example outputs we'll attach
PIPELINE_ID=ci-8421
COMMIT_SHA=fa1b2c3d4e5f
# the CI job prints: kubectl apply -f rolebinding-staging-demo.yaml --record
```
artifacts-bot: Uploaded artifact: ci-8421.log (sanitized). Uploaded artifact: cloudtrail-putrolepolicy.csv (sanitized).
harry_oncall: For the auditor mapping CSV we'll create mapping.csv with columns: artifact_filename, control_refs (SOC2/ISO), brief_evidence_note. Keep each note one sentence. Example: rolebinding-diff.patch, SOC2 CC6.1; ISO A.9.2: shows the IaC change and diff linking commit SHA to applied rolebinding.
jess_sec: Important: scrub PII, customer IDs, IPs, and internal hostnames. Use infra/tools/scrub-ids.sh and then run a quick grep for known patterns. Document the sanitizer commands in README.
auditor_sam: Please also include the emergency access / break-glass proof if there was any privileged apply (who approved, runbook ID). If none, state "no emergency access used for this demo."
leo_platform: We'll include a short timeline.txt (one-paragraph): commit -> CI trigger -> pipeline logs -> kubectl apply -> audit log timecodes -> CloudTrail events -> KMS state verification. Also a 60s MP4 showing the replay and a text file with the exact commands used.
harry_oncall: Schedule: I can run the rehearsal Monday 10am PT. Packaging target: artifacts + mapping.csv + timeline + mp4 by end of day Monday.
jess_sec: Thanks. One more ask from the auditor: include SHA and pipeline URL for traceability. If URL can't be public, include an internal link and the pipeline console output (sanitized).
auditor_sam: That sounds good. The CSV crosswalk should map to SOC2 CC6.x and CC7.x and to ISO 27001 clauses A.9 / A.12 where appropriate. A single-line justification per artifact is enough.
